research_rationale: Executive Order 11298 of August 14, 1966 (31 FR 10915), Prescribing the Interest Rate for Deposit of Savings of Members of the Uniformed Services, is a single paragraph. Acting under section 1035 of title 10, United States Code, as amended by the Act of August 14, 1966, it prescribes that amounts deposited by members of the uniformed services under that section accrue interest at ten percent per annum, compounded quarterly, and states that the order is effective September 1, 1966. The held Federal Register page text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11298.txt, GPO Federal Register of August 17, 1966) carries the heading directly above the paragraph, and the order has no other paragraph. The September 1, 1966 sentence is a start date, not an end. A search of the held corpus for the number EO 11298 finds only the order's own Federal Register page and the 1989 OFR codification (jobs/ofr-codification-1989/output/texts/EO_11298.txt). The OFR executive-order catalog records no disposition note for the order, and the three bounded searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog; coverage notes read) report no hit that amends, revokes or supersedes it. The U.S. Code release point 119-121 (Office of the Law Revision Counsel, edition current through 2026-10-09; changes enacted between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-14 are not reflected in that edition) prints the order as a note to 10 U.S.C. 1035 with no ending statement. The held text of 10 U.S.C. 1035(b) (jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t10-s1035.txt) provides that interest at a rate prescribed by the President, not to exceed 10 percent a year, accrues on amounts deposited under that section, so the statute the order implements remains in force and the prescribed rate equals its ceiling. The same held section text still provides special treatment for members in a missing status during the Vietnam conflict, the Persian Gulf conflict or a contingency operation, and its amendment notes record a 1991 amendment (Pub. L. 102-190, section 639(a)), so the deposit program was still being legislated after 1973. The 1989 codification prints an editorial note that on January 26, 1973 a terminal date of March 28, 1973 was prescribed by DOD Instruction 1348.15; the earlier-end check below tests that note and explains why it does not end the order. The order is operative on 2026-10-14.
savings_reason: No clause is terminated; the rate prescription continues, and no later order or statute supplying a different rate is held.
earlier_end_check: The order states no end date, event or condition; its only date, September 1, 1966, starts it. Held texts naming EO 11298 record no revocation, supersession or amendment. The 1989 OFR codification (jobs/ofr-codification-1989/output/texts/EO_11298.txt, an OCR text of the Government Printing Office volume, not the original) prints an editorial note under the order that on January 26, 1973 a terminal date of March 28, 1973 was prescribed by DOD Instruction 1348.15. That Instruction is not held, and the note does not say that the President's rate prescription was revoked or amended. It records a Department of Defense issuance, an administrative act under the joint regulations that 10 U.S.C. 1035(a) assigns to the Secretaries concerned, not a presidential instrument. The held evidence does not show that the terminal date was a date for the rate command: the order itself limits nothing to a period, the held statute text has since been amended to address deposits by members during the Persian Gulf conflict and contingency operations, so a presidentially prescribed rate remained needed after March 28, 1973, and no later presidential rate prescription is held. I therefore do not treat March 28, 1973 as an end of this order. What the Instruction itself ended (deposits in the then-current program period) is not established by held sources, and that does not change the state of this command, which applies to any amounts deposited under section 1035.
scope_check: The order is one paragraph with one operative command (the ten percent per annum rate, compounded quarterly, for amounts deposited under 10 U.S.C. 1035) and one effective-date sentence. The packet inventory has one clause, EO:11298#whole, covering both, and I confirmed it complete against the held page text.
independent_command_check: There is one command. The effective-date sentence only dates the start of that command and is not an independent command; the order has no report, deadline, delegation or revocation clause.
savings_check: No clause is terminated, so there is nothing to save and no residual effect is claimed.

research_rationale: Executive Order 11438 of December 3, 1968 (33 FR 18085), Prescribing Procedures Governing Interdepartmental Cash Awards to the Members of the Armed Forces, issued under 10 U.S.C. 1124(b) and (e) and 3 U.S.C. 301, has four numbered sections. Section 1 allows honorary recognition or a cash award for a suggestion, invention or scientific achievement of a member of the armed forces adopted by another executive department or agency, by the Secretary of Defense or, for the Coast Guard when not operating as a service in the Navy, the Secretary of Transportation. Section 2 lets the adopting agency recommend an award and requires awards under regulations of the two Secretaries. Section 3 caps a cash award at $25,000. Section 4 requires funds to be transferred from the recommending agency and procedures to be prescribed by the Civil Service Commission when several agencies benefit. The dossier's two-clause inventory ran sections 1 through 3 together, so I corrected it to four clauses with exact spans in the held Federal Register text. Later events, all amendments that leave the clauses continuing: (1) Executive Order 12107 of December 28, 1978 (44 FR 1055), section 2-101, lists EO 11438 among the orders in which Office of Personnel Management is substituted for Civil Service Commission, effective January 1, 1979 under section 2-404; in EO 11438 that reference appears only in section 4. (2) Executive Order 13286 of February 28, 2003 (68 FR 10619), section 63, strikes the Secretary of Transportation in sections 1 and 2 and the Department of Transportation wherever it appears in sections 2 and 4, inserting Homeland Security, effective March 1, 2003 under section 92. The packet's chain also lists EO 12977 of October 19, 1995 as an amending actor; its held text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12977.txt) does not contain the number 11438 and the source-ladder queue file attributed to it holds pages of EO 13286, so it is not a later event. The U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition current through 2026-10-09; changes between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-14 are not reflected) prints the order, as amended by EO 12107 and EO 13286 section 63, as a note to 10 U.S.C. 1124 with no ending statement. The held text of 10 U.S.C. 1124 (jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t10-s1124.txt) still authorizes these cash awards and limits them to $25,000, and the held current 5 CFR 451.101(b) (jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/cfr-t5-451.101.txt) states that section 4 of E.O. 11438 requires the Office of Personnel Management to prescribe procedures for covering the cost of a cash award recommended by more than one agency. The bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog (coverage notes read) show no revocation or supersession. The order is operative on 2026-10-14.
savings_reason: No clause is terminated; all four sections continue as amended, so no savings or residual question arises.
earlier_end_check: The order states no end date, event or condition and has no effective-date or expiry sentence. Held texts naming EO 11438 record two amendments (EO 12107 and EO 13286, both substitutions of an officer or department), the held Code note prints the order as continuing, and the held current CFR cites section 4 as a present requirement. No earlier revocation, supersession or own-terms end is held. The packet chain's EO 12977 entry is not a separate instrument (see the rationale).
scope_check: I corrected the dossier inventory (whose first clause ran sections 1 through 3 together) to four clauses, one per numbered section, with absolute spans in the held text file: section 1 861-1527, section 2 1527-2479, section 3 2479-2729, section 4 2729-3552. The authority recital before section 1 states the legal basis and commands nothing.
independent_command_check: Section 1 is a permission for awards by two named Secretaries; section 2 is a recommendation procedure with a regulation-making duty on the Secretaries; section 3 is a $25,000 limit on awards; section 4 is a funding-transfer rule with a procedures-prescribing duty. Each is separate and continuing; none is a one-time act, deadline or report.
savings_check: No clause is terminated, so there is nothing to save; the two amendments are recorded as later events on the clauses they touch.

research_rationale: Executive Order 11446 of January 16, 1969 (34 FR 803), Authorizing the Acceptance of Service Medals and Ribbons from Multilateral Organizations Other Than the United Nations, is a single paragraph. The President authorizes the Secretary of Defense (for members of the Army, Navy, Air Force and Marine Corps) and the Secretary of Transportation (for members of the Coast Guard when it is not operating as a service in the Navy) to prescribe regulations for acceptance of medals and ribbons offered by multilateral organizations other than the United Nations, and requires that a determination that service for such an organization is a justifiable basis for acceptance be made with the concurrence of the Secretary of State. Executive Order 13286 of February 28, 2003 (68 FR 10619, 10629), section 62, amends the order by striking the words the Secretary of Transportation and inserting the words the Secretary of Homeland Security; section 92 of that order states that it becomes effective on March 1, 2003, so the amendment took effect on March 1, 2003. Under the strike-and-insert ruling the clause continues, amended. The packet's chain also lists EO 12977 of October 19, 1995 as an amending actor, but its held text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12977.txt) does not contain the number 11446, and the source-ladder queue file attributed to it holds pages of EO 13286, so I do not treat EO 12977 as a later event. The OFR executive-order catalog lists only the amendment by EO 13286. The U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition current through 2026-10-09; changes between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-14 are not reflected) prints the order, as amended by EO 13286 section 62, as a note to 5 U.S.C. 7342 with no ending statement. The bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog (coverage notes read) show no revocation, supersession or other amendment. The order is operative on 2026-10-14.
savings_reason: No clause is terminated; the authorization continues as amended by EO 13286 section 62, and no residual or accrued effect is separate from it.
earlier_end_check: The order states no end date, event or condition and has no effective-date or expiry sentence. Held texts naming EO 11446 record one amendment, EO 13286 section 62 (effective March 1, 2003), which changes the Coast Guard officer named and ends nothing; no earlier revocation or supersession is held, and the apparent EO 12977 entry is not a separate instrument (see the rationale).
scope_check: The order is one paragraph. The packet inventory has one clause, EO:11446#whole, and I confirmed against the held page text that it covers the whole operative paragraph, including the Secretary of State concurrence sentence.
independent_command_check: The paragraph contains one continuing authorization (to prescribe regulations for acceptance of medals and ribbons) with an attached concurrence condition on determinations; the concurrence sentence qualifies the same authorization and is not a separate performed command, deadline or report.
savings_check: No clause is terminated, so there is nothing to save; the amendment by EO 13286 is recorded as a later event on the continuing clause.

research_rationale: Executive Order 11485 of October 1, 1969 (34 FR 15411), Supervision and Control of the National Guard of the District of Columbia, has five sections. Section 1 authorizes and directs the Secretary of Defense to supervise, administer and control the Army and Air National Guard of the District of Columbia while in militia status, with the Commanding General reporting to him and the Secretary able to order out the Guard to aid civil authorities subject to the President's direction. Section 2 makes the Attorney General responsible for advising the President on alternatives for use of the Guard and for establishing law enforcement policies after consultation with the Secretary of Defense. Section 3 provides that the President appoints the Commanding General and the Adjutant General on recommendations of the Secretary of Defense after consultation with the Attorney General. Section 4 authorizes delegation to subordinate officials. Section 5 supersedes Executive Order No. 10030 of January 26, 1949. Sections 1 through 4 are operative on 2026-10-14. Section 5 was performed when the order issued: the order has no effective-date sentence, so I record 1969-10-01, the date of signing (the instrument was filed for publication the same day), as the date of the supersession, with the later Federal Register publication date as the alternative reading. A search of the held corpus for the number EO 11485 finds the order's own Federal Register page, the 1989 OFR codification (jobs/ofr-codification-1989/output/texts/EO_11485.txt, which prints the five sections with no editorial note) and two source-ladder queue files created for EO 10030; no amendment, revocation or supersession of EO 11485 is held. The OFR executive-order catalog records only that the order supersedes EO 10030. The bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog (coverage notes read) have no hit for this order, and the packet's term leads for section 1 are report-duty wording, not an end. This is the established route in which the held original, no held later instrument and the three bounded searches support the current predicate; I do not rely on any held current-law text for this order.
savings_reason: Section 5's supersession of EO 10030 was complete when the order issued and gave rise to no continuing right; sections 1 through 4 continue and carry the order's operative content.
earlier_end_check: The order states no end date, event or condition. The machine term leads attached to section 1 are the report duty of the Commanding General, which has no date and ends nothing. The OFR catalog and the held texts name no revocation, supersession or amendment of EO 11485. The only end in the order is section 5, which supersedes EO 10030 and was performed on issuance.
scope_check: The packet inventory has five clauses, one per numbered section, and I confirmed it against the held page text: the authority recital before section 1 states the legal basis and commands nothing, and sections 1 through 5 are the whole operative text.
independent_command_check: Section 1 (Secretary of Defense supervision and control), section 2 (Attorney General responsibilities), section 3 (presidential appointments on recommendation), section 4 (delegation authority) and section 5 (supersession of EO 10030) are independent commands. Section 5 is a one-time supersession performed on issuance; the other four are continuing.
savings_check: Section 5 is the only terminated clause and its effect (EO 10030 no longer governs) needs no savings; I found no pending action, accrued right or transitional rule in the order's text.
